Wiring Listeners into app.js

One more side-effect import, in app.js rather than server.js, so listeners register under supertest too.

events/index.js only registers listeners once something imports it — so something has to. That import goes in app.js, not server.js:

// Figure 5.7: registering listeners the moment the app module loads (src/app.js, excerpt)
import routes from './routes/index.js';
import notFound from './middleware/notFound.js';
import errorHandler from './middleware/errorHandler.js';
import './events/index.js';

This leans on the same app.js/server.js split CLAUDE.md's Architecture conventions call out: app.js builds the Express app and exports it, server.js imports that app and calls .listen(). The integration tests introduced in Lesson 3 import app.js directly through supertest, and never touch server.js or call .listen() at all — so if this import lived in server.js instead, listeners would work when the app runs for real but silently never register under test, and a test creating a ticket would have no way to notice a broken listener. Importing ./events/index.js from app.js means every route the app exposes runs with listeners registered, whether that app is reached through a real port or through supertest.
